#3196. Apple releases beta 2 for iPadOS 27.3, watchOS 27.3, and more

Update, 6:15 p.m. ET: Apple has now released beta 2 for tvOS 27.3 (24K5298d) and HomePod 27.3 (24K5298d).

Apple has just released beta 2 for iPadOS 27.3, watchOS 27.3, visionOS 27.3, and more. It’s available for developers, but a public beta will likely follow in the next couple days.

Two weeks ago Apple introduced an exciting wave of beta updates as iOS 27.3 and companion releases introduced many new features.

Siri AI upgrades are a big focus in 27.3, with new languages, Siri Recap, and advanced in-app actions. There’s also a preview of new third-party app capabilities for Siri.

The all-new Health app has returned in iOS and iPadOS 27.3, this time with the expectation of launching in the public release. Fitness also adds a new Gym Strength program.

Apple Music now has a Selfie Sing feature for creating personal karaoke videos, and an improved lyrics view. Safari adds Vertical Tabs, Adaptive Dark Mode, and more.

That’s just a sampling of the new features in beta 1. And now today, beta 2 is here for iPadOS 27.3, watchOS 27.3, visionOS 27.3, and more.

We’re expecting to see additional new features and refinements today, like video podcasts being added to the Apple TV app. We’ll keep you posted on everything noteworthy we discover.

watchOS 27.3 has one of my personal favorite new features in Siri Recap, so I’m curious to see if Apple keeps refining the experience throughout the beta in response to user feedback.

Have you found anything new in beta 2 for iPadOS 27.3 or another update? Let us know in the comments.

#3195. Best Black Friday Nintendo Switch deals in 2026 — LIVE updates from Tom’s Guide’s biggest gaming fans

Black Friday deals are ten days away. But don't wait around — early Black Friday Nintendo Switch deals are already popping up all over the web. This is the second day of our live Black Friday Nintendo Switch deals coverage, and I'm here to share the best of the best deals right as they appear — leading all the way up to the big event.

I'm a huge Nintendo fan myself, and I have a thousand hours racked up on my Nintendo Switch console to prove it. I'm also always on the lookout for price drops, because who doesn't like getting one of the best Nintendo Switch 2 games for less?

Welcome! We're a day closer to Black Friday and a day closer to full access to all the best Black Friday Nintendo Switch deals. In the meantime, I'm here to share the best savings with you live — so you can beat the rush and get your holiday shopping sorted before everyone else.

First things first... here's the best way to get yourself a Nintendo Switch 2 console right now. This bundle includes a Nintendo Switch 2, a copy of Mario Kart World and a 3-month Nintendo Switch Online membership. Compared to buying everything individually, you're saving $37.

We were hugely positive about this device in our Nintendo Switch 2 review, since it's just about the perfect upgrade from the original Nintendo Switch — with stronger performance, a bigger and better display and better controllers. You also get access to a stellar library of the best Nintendo Switch 2 games and the best Nintendo Switch games as well. Oh, and you can play everything at home on the big screen or on the go!

Something important to note here is that Nintendo has confirmed it will sell the Nintendo Switch 2 Mario Kart World bundle for $499 starting November 22. That's $50 off, saving you $80 in total — and bringing the bundle back down to its original, pre-price hike MSRP. But if you don't want to wait, or want to ensure you get one before they sell out, now is still a good time to buy.

This is one of my favorite Nintendo Switch deals ahead of Black Friday. This gaming headset is shockingly good for just $14, and we gave it a 4.5-star rating in our Turtle Beach Airlite Fit review. The sound quality is excellent, and they're both comfortable to wear and easy to use. My colleague Nikita Achanta wrote that "This is a budget headset that performs like a premium one."

One of the best Nintendo Switch 2 controllers we've tested has a sneaky hidden discount right now. It's the Turtle Beach Rematch, and it offers the same battery life as the Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller — while costing less than half the price.

This deal currently only applies to the black and yellow Super Mario Star variant of the controller (add it to your cart to see the discount.) You can also get the Invincible Mario variant pictured above on sale for $50.

Looking for a gift for someone who loves Animal Crossing: New Horizons on Nintendo Switch? Or maybe you're already a fan and are looking for your next obsession. I lovingly refer to Hello Kitty Island Adventure as the second best island-themed cozy game on Switch (behind Animal Crossing); it's one of the only games that has managed to scratch the same itch for me.

In this game, you'll jet off to a deserted island and work to rebuild it into a paradise. It's packed with quests to complete and lots of options for customization. Hello Kitty Island Adventure is continuously being updated with new content, features and events — and it's also super cheap right now as it's on sale for just $19.

Want to enjoy some intense soccer action over the holiday season? The latest game in the EA Sports FC series, EA Sports FC 27, is on sale with 50% off just ahead of Black Friday. I can't call it a surprising deal, but it's still a good one!

New to FC 27 is The Grounds mode, which lets you create an avatar and then take on the world in online matches. Otherwise, it's the same game that fans know and love. Compared to the other consoles, playing on Switch 2 means you'll lose a bit of visual prowess — and gain the option to play portably.

It's not currently on sale, but you don't want to miss this Nintendo Switch 2 game. I'm calling it: it's going to be the most popular and sought after Nintendo title this holiday. Our The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time review was pretty much nothing but positive, praising the game's gorgeous visuals and music, as well as the handy quality-of-life upgrades.

Want the best sound possible for your Nintendo Switch? The best gaming headset we've tested, the SteelSeries Arctis Nova 5, is on sale with $40 off right now. While it doesn't offer active noise cancelation, it ticks every other box — it's super comfortable to wear, the battery lasts up to 60 hours and you get 360° spatial audio that makes all your games feel even more immersive. The lowest price ever for these headphones is $79, but $40 off is still a good discount.

If you're looking for Switch game deals, Walmart is a good place to check. For example: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild is on sale for $46 at Walmart right now. This game is approaching its ten-year anniversary, but even today, it's still a must have for every Nintendo gamer. It'll keep you entertained well into the new year, since it offers dozens of hours of content — and it's cheaper compared to the shiny new Zelda release, Ocarina of Time.

Sonic X Shadow Generations is one of the best Nintendo Switch 2 games you can buy. And thanks to this discount, it's also one of the cheapest options on our best-of list. This title remasters one of Sonic's finest games, and adds new content to boot. The new levels feature a storyline focused on everyone's favorite edgelord — Shadow the Hedgehog. And the soundtrack in this game is so good that it's worth the price of admission alone.

If you own lots of Nintendo Switch game cards, keep them all organized in this case from Jsaux! It makes it easier to take all your favorites with you while you're traveling. There's space for 40 games in here, as well as MicroSD cards. And since Switch and Swich 2 game cards are the same size, this case works for both.

Super Mario Odyssey is great, but Super Mario Galaxy might be even better... and this deal gets you double the fun for a similar price. The excellent 3D platformers Super Mario Galaxy and Super Mario Galaxy 2 have been ported from Wii to Switch, and they feel better than ever to play now. With this Walmart deal, you can get them both in one package for $15 off.

Running out of space for your digital games? You can add more space with this 512GB MicroSD Express card from Samsung. It's currently 33% off and on sale for $99. The lowest price ever for this one is $74, but since storage prices are generally on the rise, that deal might not come back any time soon.

This isn't the biggest discount out there, but Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream is my second favorite game of 2026. (My #1 is Rhythm Heaven Groove, in case you were wondering.)

I've been waiting years for a sequel to Tomodachi Life on 3DS, and Living the Dream brought pretty much everything I could ask for. This game lets you make your own Mii characters based on whoever you want — then you simply observe all the mischief they get up to. Your Miis can form their own relationships, move in together and even fight with each other. There are lots of options for clothing and decorations, too.

It's not the most exciting thing you can buy, but I highly recommend a screen protector for your Nintendo Switch 2. It could be a lifesaver if you hate getting scratches on your console's screen! This deal from Jsaux comes with a pack of three, so you can share with a buddy (or have multiple attempts if you struggle with installation...)

Here's a deal I wasn't expecting! Pokémon Legends Z-A is on on sale for $20 off ahead of Black Friday. Although it released last year, it's still the latest title in the mainline Pokémon series and will surely be on a lot of wish lists this holiday. Amazon and Walmart both offer this deal, but you have to add the game to your cart to see the discount.

Check out our Pokémon Legends Z-A review, where our tester named it his favorite Switch 2 game yet. The new live battle formula is an excellent shake up for the series, and the story is extremely memorable to boot.

If you don't want to damage your Switch 2 in transit, using a protective case is a good idea. And not only is this one affordable at less than $20 — it's also adorable! It features Kirby and his friend Waddle Dee surrounded by tasty treats. There's also storage for 10 game cards on the inside and a mesh pouch for accessories.

Assassin's Creed Shadows came out last year to glowing reviews, and we ourselves awarded it 4-stars. It brings back classic stealth mechanics while introducing new ones, combining the best of the older and RPG titles. Feudal Japan is extremely fun to explore whether you're parkouring or riding your horse.

You play as Yasuke (a samurai) and/or Naoe (a shinobi), and their different fighting styles and tactics enrich combat. Conduct a frontal assault or hide stealthily while taking advantage of the shadows. Assassin's Creed Shadows runs well on the Switch 2, too, making this deal a must-have!

Overcooked! and Overcooked! 2 are two of our favorite couch co-op games — and the All You Can Eat edition which includes both titles is currently available for just $32 at Amazon.

In this (highly addicting) cartoon cooking simulator, you and up to three other players must cook and deliver dishes in quick succession — the quicker you are, the more tips you earn. Chop, dice, slice, steam, fry, bake, rinse and repeat, and don't forget to wash those dishes and put out the fires lest they burn your kitchen down!

Final Fantasy VII Rebirth is, without a doubt, one of the best JRPGs out there, and you can now play it on the Switch 2. We awarded the game 4.5-stars in our review, praising its incredible graphics, engaging storylines, fun combat mechanics, and huge worlds that are ready to be explored.

Wondering how the (formerly) PS5 exclusive runs on the Switch 2, especially compared to the PS5 Pro? Check out our article outlining the differences! And once you're done, don't forget to snap up this deal as soon as possible.

EA Sports FC 27 is the latest instalment in EA Sports' annual soccer simulation series. It adds a new "The Grounds" mode, alongside fan-requested upgrades to staple modes like Ultimate Team and Career Mode. It remains the most authentic recreation of the biggest sport on Earth you can play.

For soccer fans and Switch 2 owners, FC 27 makes for a great gift — and that too at 50% off? Who are we to say no to such a killer deal!

If you want an ergonomic controller that not only cradles your Switch 2 for a more comfortable experience, but also features the latest tech to give you a competitive edge, you need the GameSir G8 Plus. It's compatible with the OG Switch, Switch 2, Android and iOS smartphones, and tablets, making it an all-in-one on-the-go solution.

We gave this wireless controller 4.5-stars in our review for its excellent design (Marvel fans will love it), long-lasting Hall Effect triggers and sticks, and customizable back buttons. It features powerful rumble motors, too, to deliver an immersive gaming experience.

"Split Fiction is the best co-op game I’ve played since It Takes Two" is what one of our editors said in his review of the game. If you're looking for a genre-defying cooperative romp, Split Fiction should be your port of call.

It's creative, inventive, colorful, and downright delightful. The main story is compelling but so is the side content. For those who enjoyed It Takes Two, or even gamers who want a compelling game to play with their partner, get this deal as it saves you $14!

Not every movie tie-in game is great, but this pack is exceptionally good. In terms of licensed tie-in games, Toy Story 2: Buzz Lightyear to the Rescue and Toy Story 3 are some of the best around! Toy Story 2 is an excellent collect-a-thon platformer, while Toy Story 3 gives you a huge sandbox world that'll make you feel like a kid playing with toys again. Those two titles alone are great enough, but in this pack you get a bunch more games besides them to check out.

Nintendo has a family-friendly image, but don't be fooled — one of 2026's scariest games, Resident Evil Requiem, is right at home on Switch 2. This game is unique in the Resident Evil series since it can be played either in first or third person all the way through. The game's two protagonists offer two different styles of gameplay — you can swap between playing as zombie-fighting veteran Leon or FBI agent Grace depending on whether you prefer action or methodical exploration.

The lowest price ever for this game on Switch 2 is $49, but $10 off is still a nice saving.

Heads up: this is not a deal for the new Mario Kart game, Mario Kart World. It's for the last game in the series, Mario Kart 8 Deluxe. MK8D is the best selling Switch game of all time, and for good reason — it provides dozens of courses to race on and pretty much unlimited hours of fun. It's also the perfect game to play with family and friends over the holiday season. It's a lot cheaper than Mario Kart World, but it's just as enjoyable.

For the ultimate cozy gaming sesh this holiday — make sure you don't go without Animal Crossing: New Horizons. This is a game I can't stop going back to, because nothing beats the feeling of booting up New Horizons and checking in with all the cute animal friends on my virtual island.

There are no concrete goals to work towards in this game, but that's what makes it so great. You're free to take it easy as you catch up with your neighbours, decorate your island and catch critters with your fishing rod or bug net.

You might be wondering, what Nintendo Switch games am I playing right now? One of the titles I have in rotation is Story of Seasons: Grand Bazaar.

I still think Stardew Valley is the best farming sim on Nintendo Switch, but Grand Bazaar is a close second. The graphics look fantastic, performance is solid and the farming gameplay is just about perfect. It's so satisfying to make a huge profit selling crops at the weekly Bazaar — and seeing a run-down village transform into a bustling hub of activity along the way.

Looking for a sleek case to carry your Nintendo Switch in? This case is hugely popular with Amazon shoppers, earning a 4.8-star rating based on over 20,000 reviews. As well as storing your console and having space for game cartridges, this case has a built-in stand — making it easier to game in tabletop mode while you're on the go!

One of the Switch 2's big new features is the option to show your face on screen during gameplay (and Game Chats with your friends.) But you need a camera to make use of it — and the Piranha Cam is the one I'd pick up. Sure, its 480p resolution isn't the sharpest around, but it just looks incredible. To figure out whether it's right for you, check out our Hori Nintendo Switch 2 Piranha Plant Cam review.

Fans waited a long time for a new Metroid Prime game, and in our books — Metroid Prime 4: Beyond stuck the landing. Not only does the game look fantastic, the levels are packed with memorable details and the combat is excellent. It's not all perfect, as you'll have to spend a decent amount of time backtracking and traversing the desert overworld. But since the game is on sale for $43 right now, it's worth picking up.

This is a deal I think just about everybody should buy. Right now you can buy a $10 Nintendo eShop gift card for $8.98 at Amazon. That means you get a little over 10% off any digital game at the Nintendo eShop! The deal is limited to two per customer, but I definitely recommend grabbing it.

Metroid Ravenous is one of the most exciting Nintendo Switch 2 game releases set for 2027. If you want to grab a copy, you can lock your pre-order in and get $10 off the physical version at Amazon right now. In this game, it's eat or be eaten — you'll need to fight off monstrous adversaries and traverse a winding maze to help Samus Aran survive.

This is an underrated Switch game for sure. I rarely hear anybody talking about Advance Wars on Switch, but it's great! This is a strategy RPG where you'll need to use your tanks and soldiers to take control of the board. It's both challenging and addicting, with plenty of variety in terms of the types of missions you'll have to complete. The character animations and colorful, diorama-style visuals look great on Switch as well.

I know, memory has gotten more and more expensive in the last two years but you may want to expand the storage in your Switch 2. Digital games add up quickly.

Fortunately, the Samsung P9 Express microSDXC is on sale for what must be the best deal I've seen for a memory card in awhile. The 512GB version is on sale for $99 right now, down from $149. You can also get the 256GB version for $47.99 down from $79.

At this point, that's a steal and you should take advantage.

If you don't prefer the Joy Con 2 controllers then you need to pick up a standard controller.

8Bitdo makes excellent controllers and the Ultimate 2 Bluetooth Controller is on sale for $51.12. Plus, it comes with a charging dock in white or black. You can also use it with the Switch or your Windows.

We are highlighting deals today, but The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time just came out, and even at full price it's worth your time. The game was and remains excellent.

The remake is $69.99, but the digital version is a little bit cheaper. If you're like me, you prefer the physical edition.

The latest installment of EA Sports' annual FC 27 soccer series is pretty good, especially if you've skipped a couple of years. The new The Grounds mode is fun and similar to The Streets in 2K. It also has great upgrades to Ultimate Team and Career Mode.

Right now, it's on sale for the Switch 2 at exactly 50% off.

If you're a racer whether its Mario Kart World or something more intense, you have to give the Joy-Con 2 Wheel grip a try.

These aren't on sale but the pack comes with two wheel grips and at $25, it won't break the bank. Plus, it's just fun and makes holding the Joy Con 2 a little more comfortable.

If you don't mind refurbished, Target has a pair of the purple/green set on sale for $10 off the regular price. It's not a huge deal but it's a bit.

These are factory refurbished so they should be as good as a new set.

Nintendo will have its own Black Friday sale that kicks off on November 19 and runs through November 22. Specifically, starting on the 19th, a number of games will be on sale in the eShop.

Here's what you'll be able to get starting on the 22nd:

PowerA makes several protection cases for the Switch 2. Not all of them are on sale, but some versions include a Zelda Hyrule crest version.

The cases hold up to 9 game cards, 2 microSD Express Cards and come with an Integrated Play Stand.

I personally have the Pikachu case - on sale for $15.99 - and find it delightful.

#3194. Use Your Year-End Review to Reach for a Promotion

Maintaining a document of your successes throughout the year gives you a starting point

Brian Jenney is the owner of Parsity, a program that helps engineers through hands-on training.

This article is crossposted from IEEE Spectrum’s careers newsletter. Sign up now to get insider tips, expert advice, and practical strategies, written in partnership with tech career development company Parsity and delivered to your inbox for free!

When I landed my first job as a software engineer, I had a simple plan: Work hard and somebody would notice. Eventually a manager would tap me on the shoulder and hand me a promotion (probably with a nice little speech).

That plan stalled my career for about five years.

I switched jobs twice, kept my head down, read a stack of programming books, and sometimes pulled 12-hour days. I was never promoted. At my third job, out of frustration, I started interviewing at other companies and almost immediately got an offer for a senior engineer role.

So I went back to my job and quit. My team was blindsided. I liked my manager and the people I worked with, and they came back with a counteroffer. Then someone from HR asked me, “Why didn’t you just ask us?”

I took the counteroffer and stayed. Three jobs in, I finally got promoted, and all it took was asking (in the most dramatic way possible).

Today, I would take a different approach.

Year-end review discussions are a great time to push for a promotion. But at most companies, raises and promotions are largely settled before the formal review conversation happens. If the year-end review is the first time your manager hears you want a promotion, you’re usually too late.

Now is a great time to start the conversation.

Engineers tend to believe good work speaks for itself. It rarely does. Your manager is juggling a team, a roadmap, and their own boss. They see a fraction of what you do, and the work they don’t see might as well not exist when raises get decided.

Perception is reality, so you have to shape it. That means learning to brag a little.

A “brag document” is a running list of what you accomplished, when, and why it mattered. Add to it every two weeks or once a month, and write each entry so your manager’s manager would understand it.

Engineers tend to write things like “migrated the billing service.” A better entry reads “migrated the billing service, which cut failed payments by 30 percent and unblocked the Q3 pricing launch.” If there’s no number, name who benefited and how.

Include the work people forget to count, too: handling incidents, mentoring new hires, interviewing candidates, and writing the docs everyone else relies on. If you helped your team adopt AI tools this year, write that down. (It counts as leadership, whether or not anyone called it that.)

The document does two jobs. It gives you ammunition when you make your case, and it gives your manager something to ctrl + c then ctrl + v when they argue for you in meetings you’ll never attend.

Bragging builds the case. Asking forces action.

If your goal is a promotion or a raise, you might ask: “What would it take for me to get to [the next level] in the next year?”

A good manager will give you an outline that can turn into a plan. Push for specifics until you have deliverables you can work toward, then send a short recap email so the plan exists somewhere besides your manager’s memory. (Managers change jobs too.)

Sometimes the answer will still be “not this year,” and the reason may have nothing to do with you.

Budgets get frozen, promotion slots get capped, and decisions get made above your manager’s head where even a manager who wants to help can’t.

Don’t read too much into that. But be honest with yourself, too. Most of the time, a no means there’s something you aren’t doing yet. Find out what it is instead of guessing for five years like I did.

Asking costs you one slightly awkward conversation. Sitting back and waiting to be noticed can cost you years.

Don’t try this at home: To better understand the risk AI slop poses to scientific publishing today, IEEE Spectrum contributor Benjamin Skuse put IEEE’s research integrity checks to the test by submitting two entirely AI-generated papers. “Science has a spam problem. And the spam filter is getting clogged up…”

Policy change doesn’t just come down to paid lobbyists—lawmakers want to hear from working experts, too. One engineer shares what he learned from his first two visits to Capitol Hill.

Could community colleges help fill the coming talent shortage in the U.S. semiconductor industry? Alternatives to four-year university degrees are a promising option for the technicians who will be needed to run new fabs.

Brian Jenney is the owner of Parsity, an online education platform that helps people break into AI and modern software roles through project-based learning and one-on-one mentorship with senior developers. Parsity helps career changers transition into software by focusing on practical skills, real-world systems, and the kind of experience companies actually look for.Outside Parsity, Brian works a senior software engineer in the SF Bay Area.Brian is also a father of three, and when he’s not working with students or building programs, you might catch him running around Lake Merritt in Oakland, California.

#3192. Apple reveals how iCloud+ increases Siri AI and Apple Intelligence usage limits

iOS 27.3 beta 2 is now available, and Apple is adding the ability for users to unlock higher usage limits for Apple Intelligence and Siri AI via iCloud+. Here’s everything you need to know.

From the start, Apple has said that some Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features have usage limits because “they rely on powerful server models.” The company previously outlined that increased access would be available across most iCloud+ subscription plans, and now we have the full details on how this will work.

Apple says the new system applies to several categories of Apple Intelligence features, including:

The usage limits are per device, not per account. This means your iPhone, iPad, and Mac each have separate allowances. Apple isn’t disclosing specific limit numbers. Instead, it says that limits can vary based on the feature, request complexity, system demand, and more.

As you near your limit, you’ll see an alert within whichever feature you’re using. For example, if you are using Image Playground, a message will appear telling you that you’ve almost hit your usage limit for the day. Once you hit the limit, you’ll be prompted to wait for it to reset or upgrade your iCloud+ plan.

If you hit your limit, basic Siri requests will still work. This includes things like setting timers and alarms. Requests that require Siri to understand personal context and perform more complex, multi-step actions, however, are subject to the limits.

For example, asking Siri to find the details of an upcoming dinner reservation in your email and add them to your calendar would count toward your daily limit.

Additionally, each device uses its own standard daily usage limit first. After that, it can tap into the additional capacity included with an eligible iCloud+ subscription:

The usage unlocked by iCloud+ is shared across all devices signed in to your Apple Account, as well as family members sharing your iCloud+ plan. The shared usage is available on a first-come, first-served basis

All limits will reset daily at the same time, and limits don’t roll over. In most cases, limits reset around midnight in your current time zone.

Apple has published a support document with more details.

#3190. macOS 27.3 includes new privacy controls for Full Disk Access and more

With today’s new macOS 27.3 beta, Apple is implementing several changes as part of this.

In a post on its developer website last month, Apple said some developers are “using Full Disk Access in ways that could put users at risk, exposing everything on their systems.” As such, it said that it would “introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action.”

In macOS 27.2, “Device Control and Data Access” is a unified toggle in System Settings, where Apple says that apps with that level of access can “view and send email, edit contacts and photos, monitor your keyboard, track websites, record your screen, control any app on your Mac, and more.”

In macOS 27.3, Apple is splitting “Device Control and Data Access” into two categories:

For the latter, users will be able to specify which apps an automation tool can access rather than granting it unrestricted control. For instance, you could give an app access to the Mail app, but not Messages.

macOS 27.3 also adds an option for users to require an app to request permission every time it needs access, rather than granting it access indefinitely.

Apple is also introducing a new menu bar indicator that will provide additional transparency when an app is controlling another app with System and App Protection Override. This is designed to let users know when an automation tool is interacting with apps and information in the background.

Crucially, Apple isn’t removing the ability to give an app Full Disk Access. If you deem it necessary, you can still give an app Full Disk Access. However, Apple is redesigning the approval process to make the implications of that decision more obvious.

macOS 27.3 will display a more detailed explanation about the protections being bypassed and the types of personal information that could be exposed.

Users can also choose to grant an app access to specific folders instead of their entire Mac. For example, an app that only needs to work with files in a particular folder won’t get unrestricted access to everything else.

Any app you’ve already given Full Disk Access will still have that access. Previously granted permissions will remain in effect, and those apps will continue functioning as they do today without any approval required.

Apple has published a new support document detailing the Full Disk Access updates.

macOS 27.3 now warns you before giving an app full disk accessThat warning prompt is pretty scary! pic.twitter.com/J2qCKVWJRx

Apple says the underlying APIs aren’t changing, but developers will need to update their apps to account for situations where users grant limited access rather than unrestricted permissions.

Finally, Apple says developers of backup apps and assistive technologies can request entitlements that allow them to maintain the same experience for new installations as before macOS 27.3. Apple has already identified popular apps that rely on these permissions, and those apps will continue working as expected without requiring an entitlement.

Developers can read more on Apple’s Developer website.

#3189. IEEE Program Schools Preuniversity Educators On Tech Topics

The TryEngineering workshops help teachers deliver engaging STEM lessons

An educator constructs a microchip model during the IEEE Making a Microchip lesson plan demonstration.

Now in their third year, the IEEE TryEngineering educator sessions continue to empower preuniversity teachers with specialized professional development programs on engineering topics and classroom-tested lessons.

This year’s sessions, held across the United States, have focused on educating teachers about artificial intelligence and semiconductor technology. One session was held in Egypt.

In all, 54 educators learned about the engineering design process this year. They received an overview of TryEngineering resources including the Making of a Microchip and Train Your Tree lesson plans.

Workshops are scheduled this year in Greece and Guatemala.

The TryEngineering program is administered by IEEE Educational Activities.

These teachers and guest speakers attended the two-day session held at the Florida Semiconductor Institute and SkyWater Technology chip manufacturing facility.IEEE Educational Activities

Central to the educator session program’s success is its university network. Host campuses welcome teachers into their facilities, where faculty provide background information about some of the technologies being taught, as well as possible engineering career paths and job opportunities for students.

This year’s sessions involved the educators in hands-on projects. Facilitators at each location were selected based on their experience in engineering education, and they worked with the TryEngineering staff on their presentations.

Sixteen teachers from nine schools participated in the session, held in Cairo. It was facilitated by Marwa Soudi, an IEEE member, and Senior Member Stamatis Dragoumanos. Both are past chairs of the IEEE preuniversity coordinating committee. GEMS provided outstanding STEM facilities for teachers, Saudi and Dragoumanos said. Participants received an overview of the Working With Wind Energy and Tall Tower Challenge lesson plans.

Another educator session is scheduled for later this year.

Educators from across the state gathered at the university’s Florida Semiconductor Institute, headquartered in Gainesville, and FSI’s NeoCity high-tech manufacturing campus near Orlando. The session was hosted by Roseanne Perez, an FSI workforce development program specialist, and Sophia Watson, FSI’s assistant director of workforce development. The two-day experience featured an inside look at microelectronics through a guided tour of a SkyWater Technology chip manufacturing facility.

Engineering instructor Mary Acken facilitated hands-on lesson demonstrations for the 15 attending teachers.

Reflecting on the workshop’s impact, one participant said the SkyWater tour was excellent, the instructors were great, and the teachers enjoyed learning from like-minded educators.

Michael Kozicki, an IEEE member, and Stefan Myhajlenko from the university’s engineering school welcomed 11 Arizona teachers to the Tempe campus.

The session was facilitated by Janet Hartkopf, an Arizona school leader and a former TryEngineering educator session participant. Hartkopf highlighted collaborative learning, the need for diverse perspectives in engineering education, and career paths.

The teachers received instruction on how to implement the hands-on lessons in their classrooms, and they toured the university’s NanoFab facility to observe microelectronics research.

“This training was amazing!” said a participant who leads an elementary after-school STEM club. “I loved the hands-on lessons and e-books, which I will definitely be using with my students. I am excited to explore all the resources on the TryEngineering website. The experts from ASU were great.”

Sixteen STEM educators attended this session, held at the university’s International Institute for Biosensing in Minneapolis. Its director, Patricia Khashayar, an IEEE member, introduced participants to the capabilities of the university’s Supercomputing Institute and Nano Center.

Under the guidance of Claire Dietz, an education and outreach coordinator, and Pam Schumacher, an instructor at St. Paul College, the teachers completed classroom-ready lessons including a photonics experiment using the Nano Center’s equipment. Schumacher attended last year’s TryEngineering educator session.

Nano Center Director Sarah Swisher, an IEEE senior member, provided an overview of semiconductor operations and highlighted growing job opportunities for the state’s young people.

The experience inspired all 16 teachers to plan student field trips to the Nano Center during the upcoming academic year, they said.

“Great class!” one participant said. “I’m excited to bring some of the TryEngineering materials back to our school.”

This year’s sessions built on the momentum from last year when, with financial support from Onsemi’s Giving Now program, nearly 80 teachers attended sessions across five U.S. states and Mexico.

Driven by that success and the demand for more, the IEEE Educational Activities Board continued its support. Upcoming global sessions are expected to expand the program’s international footprint.

“I appreciated the time to collaborate with peers on how to implement hands-on lessons,” one participating teacher this year said. Some participants said they planned follow-up visits with the experts and campus tours.

You can learn more about the sessions by emailing TryEngineering.

Debra Gulick is director of IEEE student and academic educational programs.

#3188. You Can Get This Micro-E-Reader for Under $60 Before Black Friday

Black Friday is usually a great time to grab a new e-reader, but the ongoing RAM crisis has made that a question mark this year: Amazon recently raised the prices of all its Kindles by around $50 and refreshed the entire lineup, which means your odds of grabbing one at a big discount are low. But you aren't totally out of luck: If you haven't noticed, micro-e-readers—I'm talking credit card-sized, with screens that measure around four inches—are all the rage in 2026, and right now, you can pick up one of them for less than $60.

If you too can see the appeal of carrying all of your books with you on a device so small you'll forget it's even in your pocket, it's a great time to jump in: The recently released Xteink X4 Classic is currently 34% off in an early Black Friday sale, but you'll need to act quickly: The discount will soon be gone.

Xteink is a Chinese startup that shook up the e-reading world last year with the launch of the X4, a super bare-bones device that made up for its lack of features and usability with a cheap sub-$70 price point. Since then, a huge online community of fans has formed, sharing tips on Reddit and even coming together to crowdsource an alternate operating system that fixed a lot of early problems. Xteink quickly followed up the X4 with a slate of other devices, including the X3 and the X4 Pro, which adds a front light and touchscreen (at the cost of screen clarity and two physical buttons).

The X4 Classic was released in September, improving on the original X4 with quality-of-life upgrades like a larger battery, relocated page-turn buttons, a real-time clock, and a tilt-to-turn-page feature. It's also 6g lighter and a millimeter thinner than the X4, though there is a trade-off involved there: It drops the USB-C charging port in favor of magnetic pogo pins that require a separate adapter (included).

These upgrades also increased the cost: The X4 Classic typically retails for $89, $20 more than the discontinued X4 and only $10 less than the X4 Pro. But right now, the X4 Classic is $59, or around 34% off, and its lowest price ever. It's a good option for those who prioritize crisp, readable text above the conveniences of a built-in light or touchscreen, as those add extra layers between the inner screen and outer glass, and provided you understand what you're getting into: These devices support only e-books without Digital Rights Management (DRM), which means you can't use it to read your existing library of Kindle books. On the plus side, there's no longer a need to worry about flashing new firmware if you don't want to, as the native version has been totally overhauled and is now one of your best options.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

No. If you find the product you're looking for with a major discount right now, get it. It's not likely to drop any lower, but it could always run out of stock. Take advantage of price matching or guarantees instead of waiting. Remember, you can always return products later if you change your mind. For the majority of products, the deal from Black Friday will be the same one on Cyber Monday.

#3187. iOS 27.3 adds new face unlock feature for iPhone Duo

In today’s iOS 27.3 beta release, Apple is introducing two changes for iPhone Duo users. Most notably, it adds a new face recognition option that lets you unlock your iPhone Duo by looking at it.

Apple is also adding an option to have your iPhone Duo lock when you close it.

You can enable the new option to unlock your iPhone Duo with the front camera in Settings, under Touch ID & Passcode, after updating to iOS 27.3. When enabled, your iPhone Duo will unlock after recognizing your face.

Use the front camera, along with a recent Touch ID or passcode authentication, to quickly unlock iPhone Duo when it’s closed. Face recognition data never leaves your device.

This isn’t Face ID. This new option on iPhone Duo uses the front camera on the outer iPhone Duo display to recognize your face. The iPhone Duo doesn’t have the hardware needed for Face ID.

Because this isn’t as secure as Face ID, Touch ID, or your passcode, Apple has implemented a few guardrails. First, the setting only works to unlock your iPhone Duo. To use Apple Pay, access your passwords, unlock apps, and do other things that require authentication, you’ll have to use Touch ID or enter your passcode.

This face recognition feature also has a time-based limitation. After 45 minutes of inactivity, you have to authenticate with Touch ID or your passcode. That is, if you go 45 minutes without unlocking your iPhone Duo, the facial recognition feature is disabled until you enter your passcode or use Touch ID.

Finally, this new feature also doesn’t work when using the iPhone Duo unfolded. When unfolded, you still have to use Touch ID or your passcode to unlock the device.

Second, iOS 27.3 adds an option to lock your iPhone Duo when you close it. You can enable this in Settings, under Display & Brightness. Once enabled, your iPhone Duo will lock when you fold, rather than transition from the inner display to the outer display.

Many iPhone Duo users (myself included) have said Apple should do this. Personally, I’ve been using a shortcut to mimic this behavior, but I’m glad to see that Apple has listened to user feedback and added a default setting for it.

EXCLUSIVE: Skydance has restructured its cable network division and named four executives to oversee programming, weeks after bringing together Warner Bros Discovery and Paramount.

The company has formed Skydance Global Cable Media, which will include such brands as Adult Swim, BET, Comedy Central, Discovery, Food Network, HGTV, ID, MTV, TLC and Nickelodeon.

This comes after Channing Dungey was handed an expanded role to oversee all of the cable networks, having previously overseen the WBD networks in addition to the television studio. She now is Chair, Skydance Global Cable Media in addition to running Warner Bros Television Group.

The new structure will see the programming teams divided into four: Unscripted Lifestyle; Broad-Based Entertainment; Talent, Music and Live; and Comedy and Animation. Watch on Deadline

Betsy Sanner Ayala, who is President and Head of Content for Food Network, will oversee Unscripted Lifestyle and now also Discovery, HGTV and Magnolia, with Joe Boyle continuing as Head of Content for Discovery, reporting to Sanner Ayala.

Jason Sarlanis, President and Head of Content at TNT, TBS and ID, will oversee Broad-Based Entertainment and also take on oversight of TLC, with Alon Orstein continuing as Head of Content for TLC reporting to Sarlanis. Sarlanis has been with the company for around a decade and actually started as SVP Development at TLC.

RELATED: Jennifer Dodge & Traci Balthazor To Oversee Animation Across Both Paramount And Warner Bros As Bill Damaschke Departs

Tina Perry, President and Head of Content at OWN, will oversee Talent, Music and Live. She is adding MTV/VH1 and BET to her portfolio, coming a day after BET President Louis Carr stepped down.

Sitarah Pendelton will continue as Head of Content for MTV/VH1, Brian Rikuda will serve as Head of BET, and Aisha Summers-Burke will continue as Head of BET Content. All report into Perry.

Adult Swim boss Michael Ouweleen will oversee the Comedy and Animation group.

He will oversee Skydance Television Animation — which includes Nickelodeon and Nickelodeon Animation Studios, Adult Swim, Cartoon Network, Warner Bros Animation, Cartoon Network Studios and Hanna-Barbera Studios Europe — and also will have day-to-day oversight of Cartoon Network and Adult Swim. Peter Girardi and Alec Botnick will oversee the studio assets of Nickelodeon Animation Studios, Warner Bros Animation, Cartoon Network Studios, and Hanna-Barbera Studios Europe and report to Ouweleen, with Botnick also overseeing programming on Nickelodeon along with Laurel Weir.

The animation divisions will continue to sell to third-party broadcasters and streamers.

Comedy Central now also will report to Ouweleen, with Ari Pearce running The Daily Show network day-to-day.

As part of the restructure Howard Lee — who was Chief Creative Officer, U.S. Networks — is exiting the company. He has been in that role since the end of 2024, but his recent day-to-day focus was overseeing HGTV.

#3182. 'Ghost Accounts' Are Putting Your Security at Risk, but You Can Protect Yourself

In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.

In all the years you've been online, you've likely created more accounts than you can remember, whether to shop on a website you made one purchase from, sign up for a newsletter you've since stopped reading, or download apps for school or work that you no longer need.

These so-called "ghost accounts"—all the old, forgotten logins that are still active but not in use—could expose your data in the event of a breach, increasing the risk of your information being used in malicious ways. That's why it's important to go through the effort to find and delete dormant accounts. Here's how to get started.

As McAfee describes, ghost accounts may retain lots of sensitive data, such as your contact details (phone numbers, emails, and addresses), purchase histories, payment details, and passwords. While this doesn't mean your information is sure to be compromised, the more places it lives, the more opportunities there are for bad actors to get ahold of it.

You're less likely to be keeping tabs on activity in older accounts, which may also have weak or reused passwords that haven't been updated in years. If that company or service experiences a data breach, not only is your stored data there exposed, but that information (including your password) can be used to access other accounts using tactics like credential stuffing and phishing. This also increases the risk of identity theft, as threat actors can use your name, birth date, and other information to open fraudulent accounts.

Unfortunately, finding and removing forgotten accounts can be tedious. If you have a password manager, the easiest way to start is to audit older items as well as look at security reports that identify weak or reused passwords, as well as data breaches that have impacted your accounts. If you've saved credentials in your browser keychain, go through the same process to find dormant accounts.

The next place to look is in your email: Search for account confirmation and verification emails as well as password resets using keywords like "verify your email," "free trial," "welcome," "confirm your account," or "sign up." Add a date filter to narrow down older accounts. Do this across all of your email addresses.

Once you've found accounts you no longer use, the next step is to deactivate or delete them, which you may be able to do through the settings or by reaching out to customer support. At the very least, remove all identifying information and change the password, and if possible, update the address to a burner using your browser's or password manager's hide-my-email feature. If you no longer have access to an old account, that doesn't mean it's been deactivated and your information removed, so you may need to reach out to customer support to find out how to access and delete it.

iOS 27.3 beta 2 arrived today, most notably giving the iPhone Duo a face unlock feature. The update also includes some design updates for Apple’s Calendar app.

When you open Apple’s Calendar app in iOS 27.3, the interface will look largely familiar to what was there before. But there are some key design changes that make the app better suited for one-handed use.

Most notably, the buttons for search and for adding a new event have both been moved from the top of the screen to the bottom.

Finally, the ‘Today’ button that takes you back to the current day has been changed to always show the actual date. So right now, it reads ‘Mon 16.’

You can reference the full side-by-side in the image above. Overall, these are relatively minor changes but they could make a big difference in everyday use.

#3180. Thom Velde Dies: Longtime Head Film Buyer For AMC Theatres Was 83

Thomas “Thom” Velde, a longtime head film buyer for AMC Theatres who also oversaw its Canadian operations, has died. He was 83. His family said he died October 31 of cancer in Rancho Mirage, near Palm Springs.

Velde spent more than a quarter-century at AMC Theatres as head film buyer, negotiating film agreements with domestic and international studios. He also oversaw AMC’s Canadian ops and real estate ventures.

He joined AMC in 1978, rising to become SVP Film Buyer of its Central Division before being promoted to SVP and managing director of AMC international film marketing in 1998. Tasked in that post with handling film buying policies in Canada, Asia, Europe and other regions, he forged relationships with film companies, distributors and government agencies around the world. He also supervised and trained film buyers for the exhibition chain.

After leaving AMC, he launched T Velde Consulting, working independently in motion picture distribution and consulting for clients including Microspace Communications and CJ America.

Velde’s family said was an avid golfer and a devoted college football fan who will remembered for his strength of character, his generosity and the way he made time for the people in his life.

He is survived by his wife, Deborah; daughters Andrea Ter-Velde (John McLoughlin) and Courtney Ter-Velde (Greg Horton); son, Sam Velde; stepsons Matthew Castillo (Crissy Castillo) and Spencer Castillo (Claire Castillo), two grandchildren and five step-grandchildren.

A celebration of life is set for 3 p.m. December 8 at Woodland Hills Community Church, with a reception to follow there. Velde’s family said donations in his memory may be made to to the Will Rogers Motion Picture Pioneers Foundation or the Motion Picture & Television Fund.

#3179. How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?

Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos

Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.

Last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun. Phobos, the Martian moon named for the Greek god of fear and panic, was transiting the solar disk. Too small to darken the pale, dust-tinged sky, but orbiting close enough to eclipse a significant fraction of the Sun, Phobos passed in less than a minute.

NASA’s Perseverance rover captured Phobos passing in front of the Sun from the surface of Mars.ASU/MSSS/SSI/JPL-Caltech/NASA

The tiny moon, with its murky origins, is an enigma, and one whose makeup and history could tell us much about Mars and the wider solar system. And now the international Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission, which successfully launched on 20 October, seeks to explore that mystery with an unprecedented series of landings on the unknown surface of Phobos.

This mission brings unusual challenges—for example, designing an orbit to study a microgravity moon orbiting a much larger planet. Engineers also had to figure out how to assess and land on this low-gravity pile of loosely assembled dirt and rock, how a rover might rove across it, and how the spacecraft might take samples and return them to Earth.

“I often say that landing on Phobos is like trying to land a balloon,” says Yasuhiro Kawakatsu, project manager of MMX at the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). “It’s very difficult to drop a balloon to the ground and prevent it from tilting or bouncing.”

Phobos is one of two small Martian moons; the other is Deimos, named after the Greek god of dread and terror. Their cosmic origins are unknown, though there are two prevailing theories. One holds that the moons were once asteroids from the belt between Mars and Jupiter, captured by the smaller planet’s gravity. In the other theory, Phobos and Deimos formed when a large celestial body slammed into Mars, sending debris into orbit. Some models suggest the pair are the last survivors from a cluster of satellites.

The enormous Stickney crater, roughly 9 kilometers across, dominates this view of Phobos taken by NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.University of Arizona/JPL-Caltech/NASA

Scientifically speaking, Phobos is considered a rubble pile, a loosely consolidated aggregate of rock and dust. Far too small to become spherical under its own mass, it’s shaped like a lumpy potato, roughly 27 kilometers in length, with only 1/1,800th of Earth’s gravity. On Phobos, a typical adult would weigh about as much as a tennis ball does on Earth.

More than 10 years in the making, MMX launched on Japan’s flagship H3 rocket from Tanegashima spaceport on 20 October local time. It will arrive at Mars in 2027 carrying scientific payloads from several space agencies, including NASA, and a new rover called Idefix developed by the French and German space agencies (CNES and DLR) in collaboration with JAXA.

Engineers assembled MMX’s modules at Japan’s Tanegashima Space Center before the spacecraft’s October 2026 launch.JAXA

MMX consists of three modules: a propulsion module to power its journey to Mars and apply the brakes to enter orbit around the red planet; an exploration module carrying the rover, sampling gear, and other scientific instruments; and a return module, attached to the exploration module, that harbors the capsule destined for a high-speed reentry into Earth’s atmosphere. After collecting samples on Phobos, the exploration and return modules will lift off together. The exploration module will then be jettisoned while the return module sets a course back home.

If all goes according to plan, MMX will deliver a 10-gram sample to Earth in the second half of 2031. But the mission will face a series of daunting challenges to reach that end point, including navigating complex orbits around Phobos and landing on its surface while Mars periodically blocks communications with Earth.

The MMX’s modular design includes the propulsion module [left] and the exploration and return modules [right].Kyodo News/Getty Images

“It’s the most complex mission I have ever seen,” says Patrick Michel, director of research at CNRS (the French National Center for Scientific Research) and co-principal investigator on Idefix.

An H3 rocket carried MMX into space on 20 October 2026, beginning the mission’s five-year journey to Phobos and back.The Asahi Shimbun/Getty Images

Once MMX reached low Earth orbit, its propulsion module’s engine fired, kicking off a nearly year-long deep-space cruise to Mars. On arrival, the spacecraft will need to fire its engines in an extended, carefully timed burn to slow down enough to be captured by Mars gravity. The propulsion module will then be jettisoned, leaving the exploration and return modules to orbit Mars.

“If something doesn’t go according to plan, MMX will fly by Mars and get catapulted into the solar system,” says Nicola Baresi, an astrodynamicist who coauthored a paper on specially designed orbits for MMX.

From that initial orbit, MMX will transition into a specially designed quasi-satellite orbit that allows it to keep pace with the small moon but also move around it. Since Phobos is too small to orbit in the conventional sense, the spacecraft will orbit Mars alongside the moon, following a clever egg-shaped path that slings MMX alternately ahead of and behind the moon. “When you’re closer to Mars, you’re accelerating with respect to Phobos, and when you’re farther from Mars, you’re decelerating. So you essentially go back and forth,” explains Baresi.

Martian Maneuvers To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.Chris Philpot

To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.

The best existing images of Phobos, from spacecraft such as NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and ESA’s Mars Express, have resolutions of only a few meters per pixel. That’s larger than Idefix, the mission’s rover, itself about the size of a microwave oven. To map the surface in greater detail, MMX will loop in front of and behind Phobos at distances ranging from 200 kilometers to less than 20 km from the surface.

During its two-year remote sensing campaign, the exploration module will use several cameras and a laser altimeter to map the surface in high resolution and look for candidate landing sites. When Mars passes behind the Sun as seen from the Earth, causing a roughly two-week communications blackout, MMX will retreat into a larger, stable orbit. After communications resume, MMX will prepare to send its first visitor down to the surface.

Before the exploration and connected return modules attempt to land, Kawakatsu says, MMX will send a scout that in Japanese is called “the first penguin,” leaping into unknown waters. For this mission, the first to leap will be the Idefix rover, named for the canine companion to Obelix in the French comics series Asterix. The exploration module will release the rover during a low-altitude pass of between 40 and 100 meters above Phobos’s surface in 2028 or early 2029.

MMX will use its TENGOO camera [left] and LIDAR laser altimeter [right] to map Phobos’s terrain.JAXA

It will be a tense moment that calls back to 2005, during Japan’s Hayabusa mission to explore the asteroid Itokawa. In a similarly designed drop, the MINERVA rover was released from an orbiter, but erroneously at 200 meters instead of the intended 70 meters. The rover missed the asteroid and, without propulsion, drifted off into deep space.

Idefix will get a slight nudge out of the exploration module toward its negligible-gravity target, freefalling and likely tumbling as it goes. It’s expected to touch down with a velocity of less than 1 meter per second. Unlike rovers that have landed on other surfaces with airbags or dedicated landing legs, Idefix will land without protection, apart from some extra padding on the solar panels due to their critical nature. The barely-there gravity of Phobos should allow the 23-kilogram rover to land softly, though exactly how this landing will play out is hard to predict.

The Idefix rover will travel to Phobos with its wheels tucked in and solar panels folded.DLR

“It will bounce probably several times,” says Stephan Ulamec, Idefix’s co-principal investigator and project manager at DLR. “It will come to rest somehow in some position.” Once it’s still, four retracted legs will deploy to right the rover autonomously, regardless of its orientation. It will then unfold its solar panels to charge its batteries for exploration tasks ahead.

A simulation shows how Idefix is expected to tumble onto Phobos, right itself using its articulated legs, and begin exploring the moon’s surface. DLR

Once operational, Idefix will roll at a snail’s pace, topping out at one millimeter per second. Its metal wheels have protruding blades like a paddle wheel, designed to gain traction in Phobos’s microgravity. “If we were to drive our rover faster, then it would actually be more like we were swimming through instead of driving across the surface,” says Cecily Sunday, a doctoral student involved in testing Idefix’s WheelCams at the Institut Superieur de l’Aeronautique et de l’Espace (ISAE-Supaéro) in Toulouse, France.

The WheelCams, a pair of cameras placed on the underside of the rover, will observe the wheels and their tracks during Idefix’s planned 100-Earth-day primary mission. The images will help researchers study the size and distribution of grains in Phobos’s regolith and how cohesive they are. How much or how little the grains stick together will greatly impact how Idefix moves. Sunday likens this to the difference between driving on dry and wet sand. “Think of trying to build a sandcastle with dry sand,” she says. “You can’t. Add water, and suddenly you can.”

The Idefix rover was mounted between the MMX spacecraft’s landing legs for the journey to Phobos.DLR

The team tested the rover’s nine-bladed wheels on a variety of materials, including Phobos regolith simulants provided by JAXA and DLR, lunar simulants, glass beads, quartz sand, and clay pebbles. “We characterize the mechanical properties of each simulant precisely, then test across the full range, with varying grain size, angularity, and even color, so we can map what we see in the WheelCam images back to actual surface properties,” Sunday says.

Despite the microgravity and Phobos’s rubble-pile nature, Sunday says Earth-based tests can approximate the rover’s motion on the surface of the small moon fairly well. While Phobos’s reduced gravity lowers the rover’s effective weight, there is also reduced pressure between the grains beneath its wheels. “As long as you’re moving very, very slowly and using the same materials and the same weight of the system, they should be representative,” Sunday says.

With four paddle-like wheels and deployable solar panels, Idefix is designed to crawl across Phobos.Ardan Fuessmann/Imago/Alamy

Idefix’s interactions with its new home will offer “sub-millimeter resolution and information on porosity, on grain size, on surface strength, on how hard is the material,” Ulamec says. “It fills a gap between remote observations from orbit and detailed observations of the return samples back on Earth.”

What Idefix finds on this rocky, rugged world will help determine how and where JAXA attempts to land the main spacecraft. Michel says the touchdown will provide ground truth for understanding of Phobos. When NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft touched down on the asteroid Bennu to collect a sample, its sampling arm surprisingly sank nearly half a meter into the loose material. But Ulamec doesn’t think Idefix will sink deep into Phobos, noting that Bennu is very different and much smaller, with a diameter of 500 meters.

Once Idefix has investigated the surface, MMX will face an even greater challenge: landing its much larger exploration module on Phobos. The spacecraft will make a controlled descent to roughly 10 meters above the surface, then drop the remaining distance in free fall. With so little gravity to pull it downward, even a small sideways motion could cause the lander to tip or bounce away. A successful, upright landing would mark the start of up to two hours on Phobos for the crucial sampling phase.

The MMX mission draws on the experience and technologies of Japan’s two Hayabusa sample-return missions, which landed on the asteroids Itokawa and Ryugu. But this mission has many more moving parts. MMX’s exploration module will use two sampling devices—a coring sampler developed by JAXA and a pneumatic sampler provided by NASA and fabricated by Honeybee Robotics, a subsidiary of Blue Origin. Data from these tools, and those carried by the Idefix rover, could answer questions about the origin of Phobos and how the Mars system has evolved.

The coring sampler uses a robot arm and a cylindrical corer designed to reach at least 2 centimeters below the surface. The arm can maneuver to find the best site for digging. “That by itself is a challenge because we’ve never done it,” Michel says. “You never know what can happen at the very sampling site itself, where you might have a boulder and the arm cannot move.”

Probing beneath the top layer will be valuable because solar radiation, galactic cosmic rays, and micrometeorites have battered and weathered the surface. The material below should offer a better record of the moon’s origins, and JAXA aims to collect at least 10 grams of it.

MMX will carry both the Idefix rover [bottom] and a robotic coring sampler [top] designed to dig beneath Phobos’s weathered surface.JAXA

The pneumatic sampler takes a different approach. Mounted on one of the lander’s legs, it will inject pure, non-reactive nitrogen gas into the surface and capture the grains stirred up. This sample could illuminate the changes Mars and its moons have undergone over time. The dual system also adds redundancy in the face of Phobos’s unknowns. “If the surface of Phobos proves to be very hard, [the coring sampler] may struggle to penetrate the ground. [The pneumatic sampler] would not experience this issue and still be able to gather material,” Kawakatsu says.

One of the most intriguing aspects of MMX is the additional possibility of collecting material from the planet below. It’s likely that Phobos has been peppered by Martian ejecta thrown into space by meteor impacts, so MMX also provides an opportunity to return the first Martian samples to Earth. Michel estimates that the samples could contain “a few hundred grains coming from Mars.” Scientists can distinguish those grains from native Phobos material by analyzing their oxygen isotopes.

That possibility raises a planetary-protection question. A direct Mars sample-return mission would have to follow strict rules to ensure that potentially living biological material from Mars doesn’t contaminate Earth. But those protocols don’t apply to MMX, even if its sample does collect grains of Martian soil. A panel of experts concluded that any microbes blasted off Mars wouldn’t survive the violent impact and ejection or the intense radiation exposure on the way to Phobos. This saved MMX from implementing expensive and time-consuming quarantine and containment protocols for the returning sample.

After landing on Phobos, MMX will have roughly two hours to collect samples from the moon’s surface before lifting off again.JAXA

During the brief surface operation, the robotic arm will deposit the samples in a storage unit, from which they’ll be transferred into a capsule aboard the return module and sealed in a vacuum. After that, lift off.

Once back in Mars orbit, the exploration module will resume its observations of Phobos and make several flybys of Mars’s other diminutive moon, Deimos, to gather data on its surface, structure, and composition. In November 2030, during a favorable alignment of Mars and Earth, MMX will begin the homeward leg of its trip. The return module will separate from the exploration module and power the voyage home, its sole objective to bring the dust of Phobos to Earth.

MMX’s sample return capsule will carry material from Phobos through Earth’s atmosphere in 2031.JAXA

Finally, in 2031, the 60-centimeter-wide sample capsule will plunge into Earth’s atmosphere at roughly 12 kilometers per second. Assuming it survives the extreme heat of reentry and lands safely in Australia, scientists will begin to tease out clues about Phobos and the early solar system. JAXA’s Institute of Space and Astronautical Science will receive and curate the samples, which will also be shared with mission partners.

“We have macroscale measurements from the spacecraft, microscale measurements with the rover, and then sample analysis,” Michel says. “So we can relate the three kinds of scales together because we have all of them.” The insights gleaned from orbital images, close-up images of the regolith, and the chemical analysis of the samples could have wider implications for our understanding of our solar system.

“MMX is a mission to understand the Mars system and shed light onto how terrestrial planets like the Earth, and maybe Mars, develop a habitable environment,” Kawakatsu says. “We strongly suspect that our terrestrial planet region formed dry, and water and organics were scattered inwards from the icy-rich outer solar system.” Mars, he says, sits at the gateway between the inner and outer solar system, making its moons valuable witnesses to the processes that shaped potentially habitable worlds.

Andrew Jones is a freelance journalist based near Helsinki. He writes about the space industry and technology with a particular focus on China's activities.

The communications blackout offers a chance to learn things about handling errors autonomously and recording and storing data autonomously that should useful for other deep space missions. I wonder what the engineers are most worried about for that phase of the mission!
